sources.name: PMC record of the ENIGMA BRCA1 and BRCA2 VCEP paper (American Journal of Human Genetics 2024, PMC11393667)
sources.description: The record returned by NCBI E-utilities for this article. PMC holds the front matter, the Summary and the graphical abstract text only: the article body, its tables and its methods are not in this record, and no open full text could be retrieved.

profile.summary: This record covers the evaluation reported in the ENIGMA BRCA1 and BRCA2 Variant Curation Expert Panel's 2024 specification paper. The panel reviewed every ACMG/AMP classification criterion for its relevance to BRCA1 and BRCA2, used statistical methods to calibrate how strong each data type's evidence is, and then tested the resulting specifications on a pilot set of 40 variants that already had ClinVar classifications. The measure of success is how many of those variants the specifications resolve or classify with more confidence. It is useful to anyone who wants to know how a gene-specific ACMG/AMP specification is built and validated, rather than to anyone comparing computational predictors.

summary_quotes.text: The VCEP reviewed American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics/Association of Molecular Pathology (ACMG/AMP) classification criteria for relevance to interpreting <italic toggle="yes">BRCA1</italic> and <italic toggle="yes">BRCA2</italic> variants. Statistical methods were used to calibrate evidence strength for different data types. Pilot specifications were tested on 40 variants and documentation revised for clarity and ease of use.
Review resolved classification for 11/13 uncertain significance or conflicting variants and retained or improved confidence in classification for the remaining variants.

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Two things. First, whether each ACMG/AMP criterion can be applied to BRCA1 and BRCA2 at all, and at what strength: the panel found that the original descriptions of 13 evidence codes were non-applicable or overlapped other criteria, and that eight codes needed their scenario of use extended or repurposed. Second, whether the resulting specifications change classification outcomes in practice, tested on variants whose existing ClinVar status was known.

quotes.text: The original criterion descriptions for 13 evidence codes were considered non-applicable or overlapping with other criteria. Scenario of use was extended or re-purposed for eight codes.
Extensive analysis and/or data review informed specification descriptions and weights for all codes.

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: The panel is a ClinGen Variant Curation Expert Panel that grew out of an ENIGMA BRCA1 and BRCA2 classification sub-group formed in 2015 as a ClinGen external expert panel, and became an internal panel to fit the Food and Drug Administration recognised process for ClinVar submissions. The pilot set is 40 variants chosen by their pre-existing ClinVar classification: 13 of uncertain significance or conflicting, 14 pathogenic or likely pathogenic and 13 benign or likely benign. How the calibration itself was done, and how the pilot variants were selected within each class, is in the article body, which is not in the record read.

quotes.text: An ENIGMA <italic toggle="yes">BRCA1/2</italic> classification sub-group, formed in 2015 as a ClinGen external expert panel, evolved into a ClinGen internal Variant Curation Expert Panel (VCEP) to align with Food and Drug Administration recognized processes for ClinVar contributions.

Specifications were applied to pilot variants with pre-existing ClinVar classification as follows: 13 uncertain significance or conflicting, 14 pathogenic and/or likely pathogenic, and 13 benign and/or likely benign.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: The pilot is scored by classification outcome, not by a continuous metric: for each of the 40 variants, whether applying the specifications resolved an uncertain or conflicting classification, and whether confidence in an already classified variant was retained or improved. The headline result is that 11 of the 13 uncertain or conflicting variants were resolved. Alongside this, the calibration step assigned evidence strengths and weights to every code using statistical methods, and the documentation was revised after the pilot for clarity and ease of use. The statistical method, the thresholds it produced and the tables holding them are in the article body and were not readable here.

facts.label: Datasets
facts.value: One pilot set of 40 BRCA1 and BRCA2 variants with pre-existing ClinVar classifications: 13 uncertain significance or conflicting, 14 pathogenic or likely pathogenic, 13 benign or likely benign. The data types behind each evidence code were also reviewed and calibrated, but the record read does not name or size those datasets.

quotes.text: Specifications were applied to pilot variants with pre-existing ClinVar classification as follows: 13 uncertain significance or conflicting, 14 pathogenic and/or likely pathogenic, and 13 benign and/or likely benign.
Pilot specifications were tested on 40 variants

facts.label: Splits
facts.value: Inapplicable as a train and test split: this is an expert specification applied to a pilot set, with no model and no held-out partition. The only division is by the variants' pre-existing ClinVar class, which sets up the three outcomes reported. How the calibration datasets relate to the pilot variants is not stated in the record read.

facts.label: Metrics
facts.value: Classification outcome counts, not a continuous score: how many uncertain or conflicting variants were resolved (11 of 13) and whether confidence was retained or improved for the rest. The calibration step produced evidence strengths and weights per code; the record read does not give the quantity those were calibrated against.

quotes.text: Review resolved classification for 11/13 uncertain significance or conflicting variants and retained or improved confidence in classification for the remaining variants.
Extensive analysis and/or data review informed specification descriptions and weights for all codes.

facts.label: Baselines
facts.value: The comparison points are human and procedural rather than computational: the baseline ACMG/AMP criteria as originally written, the panel's own pre-existing ENIGMA research classification process, and the variants' pre-existing ClinVar classifications. The record read states that aligning the research process with the ACMG/AMP guidelines exposed gaps in both.

quotes.text: Alignment of pre-existing ENIGMA research classification processes with ACMG/AMP classification guidelines highlighted several gaps in the research processes and the baseline ACMG/AMP criteria.
variants with pre-existing ClinVar classification

facts.label: Leakage controls
facts.value: It may be in a source that could not be read. The pilot variants had pre-existing ClinVar classifications, so the panel knew the prior answer when applying the specifications, but whether curators were blinded, and whether the pilot variants were excluded from the calibration data, is not stated in the record read. The article body was not available.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Summary; the article body is not in the PMC record

facts.label: Uncertainty
facts.value: Not in the record read. The Summary says statistical methods were used to calibrate evidence strength but gives no interval, replicate or sensitivity analysis, and the pilot outcome is reported as a count of 11 of 13. Any uncertainty on the calibrated thresholds would be in the article body, which could not be read.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Summary; the article body is not in the PMC record

facts.label: Entity type
facts.value: One germline sequence variant in BRCA1 or BRCA2, classified under the ACMG/AMP framework. For the specification work itself, the unit is an evidence code: 13 whose original descriptions were judged non-applicable or overlapping, and eight whose scenario of use was extended or repurposed.

quotes.text: The original criterion descriptions for 13 evidence codes were considered non-applicable or overlapping with other criteria.
relevance to interpreting <italic toggle="yes">BRCA1</italic> and <italic toggle="yes">BRCA2</italic> variants

facts.label: Organisms
facts.value: Human. The work concerns germline variants in the BRCA1 and BRCA2 hereditary breast and ovarian cancer genes.

quotes.text: The ENIGMA research consortium develops and applies methods to determine clinical significance of variants in hereditary breast and ovarian cancer genes.
sequence changes in the BRCA1 and BRCA2 breast cancer risk genes

facts.label: Assays
facts.value: Not named in the record read. The Summary says only that evidence strength was calibrated for different data types, without listing them.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Summary; the article body is not in the PMC record

facts.label: Allowed inputs
facts.value: Whatever the specified evidence codes permit, which the record read does not enumerate. This is an expert curation framework rather than a prediction task, so there is no restriction on inputs comparable to a model benchmark; the specification defines which evidence types may be used and at what strength.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Summary; the article body is not in the PMC record

facts.label: Adaptation
facts.value: Inapplicable. Nothing is trained, fitted or tuned on examples in the sense a model benchmark means: the panel calibrated evidence weights by statistical analysis and then applied the written specifications by expert review, revising the documentation after the pilot.

strengths.text: Evidence strength was calibrated statistically rather than assigned by convention, and the panel reports that this calibration was what justified the utility and strength of each data type for gene-specific use.

quotes.text: Calibration of evidence strength was key to justify utility and strength of different data types for gene-specific application.

strengths.text: The specifications were piloted before release, on a deliberately mixed set of 40 variants spanning uncertain or conflicting, pathogenic and benign prior classifications, and the documentation was revised in response.

quotes.text: Pilot specifications were tested on 40 variants and documentation revised for clarity and ease of use.
13 uncertain significance or conflicting, 14 pathogenic and/or likely pathogenic, and 13 benign and/or likely benign

strengths.text: The review was willing to find fault with both inputs: it reports gaps in the panel's own pre-existing research process as well as in the baseline ACMG/AMP criteria, and judged 13 evidence codes non-applicable or overlapping.

quotes.text: highlighted several gaps in the research processes and the baseline ACMG/AMP criteria
The original criterion descriptions for 13 evidence codes were considered non-applicable or overlapping with other criteria.

limitations.text: The pilot is 40 variants, two genes and one expert panel, so the reported resolution rate rests on 13 uncertain or conflicting variants. It is a demonstration that the specifications work, not a measurement of how often they resolve uncertainty at scale.

quotes.text: Pilot specifications were tested on 40 variants
Review resolved classification for 11/13 uncertain significance or conflicting variants

limitations.text: The panel evaluated its own specifications on variants whose prior ClinVar classifications were known, and the record read says nothing about blinding or about whether the pilot variants were independent of the calibration data.

quotes.text: Specifications were applied to pilot variants with pre-existing ClinVar classification
Statistical methods were used to calibrate evidence strength for different data types.

limitations.text: Nothing here is reusable as a benchmark: there is no score, no held-out set, no code and no released evaluation data. The outcome is a written specification, which the authors describe as publicly accessible protocols for genetic diagnosis.

quotes.text: These publicly accessible protocols can now be used for improved genetic diagnosis and thereby patient management.

limitations.text: The article is not open access. The copyright line reserves all rights, including for text and data mining and AI training, and no open full text could be retrieved, so this page rests on the Summary alone.

gaps: Only the Summary was readable. The PMC record for this article holds the front matter, the Summary and the graphical abstract text; the body, Table 2 and the methods are not in it, Europe PMC's full text service returned HTTP 500, and the article is not open access.

The calibration thresholds the record's stored protocols refer to, including the BayesDel thresholds for BRCA1 and BRCA2 and the generic threshold assignments, could not be read and are therefore absent from this page.

no_run_guide_reason: There is nothing to run and no instructions to read. This is an expert panel's variant classification specification and a 40-variant curation pilot: no code, no evaluation data and no scoring procedure is released, and the article's full text was not available.

notes: This page is written from the Summary alone and should be revisited if the full text becomes readable. The PMC record for PMC11393667 holds only front matter, the Summary and the graphical abstract text; Europe PMC's fullTextXML returned HTTP 500, the PMC open access package service returned no record for this article, and the article's own copyright line reserves all rights, so its bytes are kept but not stored. Consequences for a human applying this. First, four of the five stored protocols on this record (BRCA1 and BRCA2 BayesDel evidence calibration and the two generic BayesDel threshold evidence-code assignments) cannot be written up from any source read, so only the pilot resolution protocol appears in the structured list. Second, the facts for leakage controls, uncertainty, assays and allowed inputs are marked unextracted rather than unreported, because they are likely to be in the article body. Third, the only counts available are 40 pilot variants (13, 14 and 13 by prior class), 11 of 13 resolved, 13 evidence codes judged non-applicable or overlapping and 8 repurposed; the 13 plus 14 plus 13 split sums to the stated 40. Fourth, the specifications are published through ClinGen as publicly accessible protocols; that registry was not fetched for this page and would be the next source to add.
